prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 218px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 147px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 1235px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 62px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 599px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 598px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"The description column is far too narrow, forcing 8–10 line paragraphs; course names and trainer names also wrap heavily, making the table tall and slow to scan."},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"Reasonably balanced with intact fees, but the course-name column is still narrow enough to split long titles into three lines and add unnecessary height."},"C":{"grade":"bad","why":"The description is squeezed into a very narrow column with 12–15 line cells, so rows become enormous and the table loses scanability; the wide fee column does not compensate."},"D":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The wide description and compact rows work well, but the fee column is too narrow: every fee breaks into amount and currency on separate lines."},"E":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Well proportioned: course names mostly take two lines, fees stay on one line, and the description is wide enough to keep paragraphs from dominating row height."},"F":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Nearly identical to E: fees stay intact, titles and durations wrap acceptably, and the long description column is balanced against the short columns."}},"best":["E","F"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"E and F are visually almost identical, so their tie is based on very small differences in column balance rather than a clear separation."}
